Cite def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure and its hypotheses; the separately cited general total-variation theorem does supply the bound. This is an inaccurate definition citation, not a claimed counterexample to the estimate.

The proof assumes complex-exponential unit modulus, differentiation and phase addition, and |exp(i theta)-1|<=|theta|. The opened real Newton–Leibniz theorem only integrates a known real derivative and establishes none of these identities. A metadata traversal of the actual deps closure finds no complex-exponential definition, entire/derivative theorem, addition theorem or Euler/modulus result. Supply those exact prerequisites and a complete Lipschitz derivation, or define the encoding and prove the identities locally. The assigned diffraction theorem already gives a local Euler/cosine-Taylor argument; that consumer does not retroactively justify its supplier.
